experiments.hypothesis: A provider-neutral capability IR plus generic synthetic counterfactual supervision can veto unsupported operations for arbitrary newly registered native/OpenAPI/MCP tools without route-specific retraining.
experiments.failure_reason: The provider-neutral compiler and authority invariants worked, but the generic synthetic learned veto rejected nearly all valid supported requests. Per preregistration it was closed without label-driven repair.
paper_relevance: negative result for synthetic learned veto

experiments.hypothesis: A registry-independent explicit request frame plus deterministic within-tool contract filtering can turn same-domain unsupported operations into empty capability sets without learned abstention thresholds.
experiments.failure_reason: The query-first typed filter preserved supported routing and runtime budget but a high-precision lexical frame left too many unsupported requests structurally unknown, allowing the raw BGE domain anchor to force a registered endpoint.

experiments.hypothesis: A frozen registry-independent multilingual semantic action ontology can classify request operation semantics before deterministic tool-local capability matching without learned thresholds.
experiments.failure_reason: The flat semantic action argmax separated ordinary OOD but was too noisy to receive hard endpoint-filtering authority, removing many valid supported endpoints while still under-rejecting same-domain unsupported operations.

experiments.hypothesis: A hierarchical executable-capability ontology with root/leaf constraints and contrastive multilingual prototypes can improve open-set membership while preserving registered execution authority.
experiments.failure_reason: The ontology remained useful as representation, but noisy root/leaf semantic projection was unsafe as endpoint-removal authority: raw BGE already met supported exact on DEV with 100% tool accuracy, while ontology filtering destroyed valid routing.

experiments.hypothesis: Preserve the frozen BGE-M3 raw top-1 as the sole positive route selector and use ontology evidence only as an asymmetric unsupported-membership veto under a fixed independent-agreement rule.
experiments.failure_reason: The negative-only ontology authority separation preserved every raw-correct supported winner and achieved 99.22% veto precision, but exact same-leaf independent agreement was too strict: veto recall was only 39.51%, leaving near-domain rejection at 26.59% and false-route at 60.49%.

experiments.hypothesis: Replace exact unsupported-leaf agreement with anchored-tool capability-set membership consensus while preserving frozen BGE-M3 as the sole positive route selector.
experiments.failure_reason: Capability-set consensus improved veto recall versus exact-leaf agreement but remained far below the open-set target and began vetoing correct supported winners; the same BGE/MiniLM ontology-projection evidence family is closed for further rule tuning on consumed DEV.

experiments.hypothesis: A small externally pretrained multilingual zero-shot classifier can judge whether a request belongs to the finite capability set registered for the BGE-anchored tool, while remaining negative-only and never selecting another endpoint.
experiments.failure_reason: The external classifier preserved supported routing but the generic OUTSIDE catch-all almost never won native multiclass normalization against concrete supported capability labels, yielding 1.85% veto recall and 98.15% false routing. Quality failed, so runtime-only optimization was not eligible.
interpretation: A 141M external multilingual zero-shot classifier is computationally plausible as a bounded verifier.
Concrete supported labels dominate a generic OUTSIDE catch-all under this multiclass formulation.
Negative-only authority again preserved route safety: zero route switches and zero authority violations.
A successor requires different membership semantics rather than label/template/threshold repair on consumed DEV.

experiments.hypothesis: Use one direct NLI sequence-pair judgment over the anchored tool's full registered capability set; preserve the frozen BGE-M3 winner on entailment and veto to NO_ROUTE on not-entailment.
experiments.failure_reason: The single aggregate set-membership hypothesis produced not-entailment for all 552 DEV queries, perfectly rejecting unsupported requests but also vetoing every raw-correct supported winner.
interpretation: The external NLI model can be fast enough at the pair level, but the aggregate membership sentence is not semantically aligned with the model's entailment behavior.
The result brackets #371: generic OUTSIDE multiclass almost never vetoed, whereas one aggregate set-entailment pair always vetoed.
A successor must change semantic decomposition rather than tune labels, wording, thresholds, or language-specific rules.

experiments.hypothesis: Judge every registered capability leaf independently with a pinned multilingual NLI model; preserve frozen BGE-M3 raw top-1 if any registered leaf is entailed, otherwise veto to NO_ROUTE.

interpretation: Per-capability decomposition is more informative than one aggregate set hypothesis.
Negative-only authority still prevents route switching and execution-authority violations.

interpretation: Pairwise supported-vs-counterfactual comparison is more balanced than the OUTSIDE-label and aggregate-set NLI extremes but still does not establish a safe membership boundary.

experiments.hypothesis: Schema-only positive views can define endpoint-local adaptive spherical regions that preserve supported natural-language requests while rejecting unsupported requests.
experiments.failure_reason: Every DEV query fell outside every learned spherical boundary; schema-synthetic positive compactness did not transfer to natural user language.
experiments.tuning_policy: No radius rescaling or positive-view rewriting from consumed DEV.

experiments.hypothesis: Same-resource hard negatives from the registered capability complement plus a low-rank anisotropic ellipsoid can preserve natural supported requests while rejecting near-domain OOS.
experiments.failure_reason: All 552 natural DEV queries lay outside the learned ellipsoids despite separation of synthetic positives and hard negatives.
experiments.tuning_policy: Do not tune margin, PCA rank, optimizer, evidence wording, or boundary criterion from consumed DEV.

experiments.hypothesis: A tied diagonal Gaussian likelihood ratio between schema positives and complement negatives can avoid absolute-boundary collapse while remaining veto-only.
experiments.failure_reason: Relative density preserved supported requests but a single Gaussian per class collapsed multimodal operation structure and under-rejected unsupported requests.
experiments.tuning_policy: No threshold, variance-floor, prior, evidence, or representation tuning from consumed DEV.

experiments.hypothesis: Registry-fixed endpoint/complement Gaussian components with log-sum-exp mixture evidence can model capability multimodality without changing positive route authority.
experiments.failure_reason: Endpoint-level mixture structure preserved supported winners but complement-negative likelihoods remained too remote from natural unsupported/OOD queries; synthetic-to-natural membership gap persisted.
experiments.tuning_policy: No threshold, covariance, variance floor, priors, components, or evidence-bank tuning from consumed DEV.

experiments.hypothesis: A threshold-free non-parametric k=3 local-neighborhood comparison over schema-positive, complement, and frozen generic background banks can avoid Gaussian assumptions and improve open-set membership.
experiments.failure_reason: Non-parametric neighborhoods improved unsupported recall versus V6C/V6D, but positive/complement natural-language manifolds still overlapped heavily and the sparse generic background bank covered little natural OOD; supported exact also fell below target.
experiments.tuning_policy: No k sweep, thresholds, neighbor weighting, background-anchor editing, evidence rewriting, or decision-order changes from consumed DEV.

experiments.interpretation: Naturalistic multilingual linear probes improve broad OOD recognition but remain insufficient for same-domain unsupported-operation membership and supported-route preservation.
Tool-specialized Tool-Embed-0.6B did not outperform same-surface BGE-M3 and missed the runtime gate.
Joint query-document relevance over registered, counterfactual, and background documents did not establish open-set membership and was far beyond the CPU runtime budget.
Historically promising GTE retrieval did not transfer to the fresh registry surface; BGE-M3 won by 16.67 percentage points while GTE retained a good CPU runtime.

A fixed alpha=0.01 unsupported-null conformal gate reached the open-set safety/runtime targets, but the scalar E5 catalog score overlapped too strongly and vetoed 87.29% of raw-correct supported winners.

End-to-end multilingual encoder fine-tuning learned tool-vs-background scope well but operation semantics generalized too weakly, especially for near-domain unsupported requests. This closes the 0.13 authoritative parser/veto formulation.

Top-1 is a poor primary product metric for multi-tool capability retrieval. Top-5 preserved every required capability on the frozen benchmark while schema-context ratio fell to 2.38% of FULL at 250 endpoints.

Canonical B1 is terminal. SR-5 and SR-10 pass the frozen utility gates on the 23-task Qwen3-0.6B controlled surface, with large schema-context reduction. This is mechanism/sanity evidence only; broad agent generalization still requires #423/#432 and final-answer quality requires #424.
